title: 第7章 全靠同行衬托第8章 保持你的格调
slug: 百世轮回词条无限累加
lines: 侍者手里拿着烫金的菜单。
他脸上的笑容有点僵硬。
因为他对面的客人，把自己打扮得像个发面馒头一样的老头，已经盯着菜单看了足足五分钟。
老杰克的手在抖。
虽然幅度很小。
但他确实在抖。
那菜单上的数字对他来说不是价格。
那是割在他心头肉上的刀子。
一份惠灵顿牛排要三个金币？
怎么不去抢！
这牛是喝圣水长大的吗？
还有这什么鹅肝酱配松露，五个金币？
老杰克感觉自己的心脏在抽抽。
他这辈子都没吃过这么贵的东西。
要是真点了这些，估计这顿饭还没吃完，他就要因为心痛而当场暴毙。
老杰克清了清嗓子。
他合上菜单。
动作很重。
像是要把那上面的价格都夹死。
他抬起头，用那种这辈子最傲慢的眼神看着侍者。
“只有这些？”
侍者愣了一下。
“先生，这是我们这一季最新的主厨推荐……”
“太油腻。”
老杰克摆了摆手。
一脸嫌弃。
“我家少爷身体抱恙，受不得这种油腻腥膻的东西。”
“那是野蛮人的食物。”
“我们要清淡的。”
老杰克伸出一根手指。
“给我来一份切成丝的土豆，要过水，不要放油。”
“再来一份白水煮的卷心菜，只要最嫩的菜心。”
老杰克咬了咬牙。
毕竟要撑场面，全是素的也不行。
“来一份牛肉丁。”
“切成指甲盖大小，要全熟，不要酱汁。”
侍者听傻了。
他在金麦穗餐厅干了三年。
见过点最贵的酒漱口的。
见过把牛排切碎喂狗的。
但来这种顶级餐厅点水煮白菜和土豆丝的，这还是头一回。
content_en:
The waiter held a gilded menu in his hand.
The smile on his face was a little stiff.
Because the customer opposite him, an old man dressed like a steamed bun, had been staring at the menu for five minutes.
Old Jack's hands were shaking.
Although the magnitude is small.
But he was shaking.
The numbers on the menu were not prices to him.
That was the knife that cut into his heart.
A steak Wellington costs three gold coins?
Why not grab it!
Did this cow grow up drinking holy water?
And this foie gras with truffles, five gold coins?
Old Jack felt his heart twitching.
He had never eaten anything so expensive in his life.
If he had actually ordered these, he would probably die on the spot from heartache before the meal was finished.
"Ahem."
Old Jack cleared his throat.
He closed the menu.
The action is heavy.
It's like trying to squeeze all the prices on it.
He raised his head and looked at the waiter with the most arrogant look in his life.
"That's all?"
The waiter was stunned for a moment.
"Sir, this is our latest chef recommendation for this season..."
"Too greasy."
Old Jack waved his hand.
A look of disgust.
"My young master is in poor health and can't bear this greasy and smelly stuff."
"That's savage food."
"We want something light."
Old Jack held out a finger.
"Bring me some shredded potatoes, soaked in water and without oil."
"Another piece of boiled cabbage, only the tenderest ones."
"Finally..."
Old Jack gritted his teeth.
After all, if you want to hold up the scene, it’s not enough to be all vegetarian.
"Have some diced beef."
"Cut it into fingernail-sized pieces and cook it well, no sauce."
The waiter was dumbfounded.
He worked at the Golden Wheat Sheaf for three years.
I've seen some of the most expensive wine to rinse my mouth with.
I’ve seen steak cut up and fed to dogs.
But this is the first time I order boiled cabbage and shredded potatoes in such a top-notch restaurant.
"gentlemen……"
